single_change: Host-side D-dependent cap on the active-core count: when rowWidth > kCacheElems (8192) and the parent launch is already core-saturated (blockCount < rowCount), cap blockCount at rowCount / residentRows, where residentRows mirrors ChooseWideFullYRows() on the host. Cap is a pure upper bound; never raises blockCount above the parent value, never drops below 1, introduces no row grouping, and leaves row ownership order and per-row kernel math byte-identical.
focus_value: blockCount = min(availableCoreNum=40, rowCount, rowCount/residentRows) for rowWidth>8192

observable_parameters.M: rows (48 on cap-active targets, 12 on the short-D control)
observable_parameters.dispatch: wide full-y path (rowWidth > kCacheElems=8192) for every cap-active shape; standard per-row path for the D=8192 control
observable_parameters.activeCoreCount: Parent 40 (device vector cores); Candidate 24 on 48x16384 fp16 and 48x12288 bf16, 16 on 48x12288 fp16, unchanged 40 on 48x32768 fp32 (residentRows=1) and unchanged 12/2/40 on the D<=8192 shapes
observable_parameters.blockCount_candidate: min(40, rowCount, rowCount/residentRows) when rowWidth>8192 and 40<rowCount, else identical to parent
observable_parameters.localRows: rowCount/blockCount base+extra split; rises from 2 to 3 (48x16384 fp16, 48x12288 bf16) or from 2 to 4 (48x12288 fp16) under the cap
observable_parameters.tileCount: ceil(rowWidth/4096): 4 at D=16384, 3 at D=12288, unchanged
observable_parameters.residentRows: 2 at D=16384, 3 at D=12288 fp16, 2 at D=12288 bf16, 1 at D=32768 (host mirror of ChooseWideFullYRows, see capcalc.txt)
observable_parameters.ownership_mapping: unchanged contiguous base/extra row split; only the divisor changed
observable_parameters.MTE2_MTE3_transaction_count: unchanged in total (2 input loads + 1 store per row per tile, every row still processed once); only the distribution across cores changes
observable_parameters.param_residency: unchanged (gamma/bias still re-read per tile in the output pass)

local.local_score_definition: median paired delta vs R31B V011 on the only shape that reached same-binary PASS; positive means the Candidate is slower
local.interpretation: The mechanism has no consistent direction. The one shape with a qualified same-binary floor (48x12288 bf16, floor 0.057) shows the Candidate 11.1% SLOWER at the median, 3 of 4 pairs favouring the Parent, and both blocks beyond the floor in the Parent's favour. The two shapes that appear to favour the Candidate (48x16384 fp16 at -16.0%, 48x12288 fp16 at +15.2% mixed) never reached same-binary PASS, and their deltas sit at or inside their own much larger floors. The short-D control confirms the cap is inactive at D=8192 and simultaneously shows this window's noise is roughly +-5% with occasional +90% outliers, larger than most cap-active deltas. Mechanistically the cap cannot reduce total work - every row is still processed once and total MTE2/MTE3 transactions are unchanged - it only removes concurrent readers, so on a bandwidth-bound wide path it is expected to be neutral at best. The data agrees.
local.residual_risk: Only one of four shapes ever produced a qualified noise floor, and its own P/C cells were far less stable than the floor run. The negative result is directionally consistent but rests on a single qualified shape; it is enough to reject V001, not enough to declare the whole D-aware blockCount family exhausted.

boundary: 2x12288 fp16 (SYNC-TOPOLOGY-CHAMPION-X V001 correctness shape; blockCount==rowCount so cap is exactly inert)
